","datePublished":"2024-07-01T08:30:03.133Z","dateModified":"2024-07-01T08:30:03.133Z","description":"Chief Strategist Keith Lerner is bullish on tech long term, but says  there are better investment opportunities now.","keywords":["AI","Big Tech","Markets","Investing"],"articleBody":"After Big Tech's meteoric rise in the stock market, valuations may be coming back down to earth. That's the concern of Truist's Chief Strategist and CIO Keith Lerner, at least. In a note last Friday, Lerner downgraded the firm's rating on the technology sector from overweight to neutral as names like Nvidia, Apple, and Google continue to drive the sector to its most extreme outperformance in decades. The stock market is incredibly narrow, with just a few mega-cap tech stocks driving the market rally. Overall, the tech sector has risen by roughly 40% since November 2023. That's about 16 percentage points higher than the S&P 500 in the same timeframe. The sector has outperformed the S&P 500 by around 11% in the last month, the highest level since 2002. According to Lerner, tech valuations are overheating in the short term, fueled by investor optimism. The tech sector's forward P/E has increased 19% just since May 1st of this year, jumping from 26x to 31x. These soaring valuations seem to be outpacing earnings growth, making now an unideal time for investors to buy in. Tech stocks are performing similarly to how they did last year, as seen in the chart below. If they continue following the same trajectory, they're likely to pull back in the next few months before rebounding again. Investors shouldn't be concerned about a tech bubble, though. Compared to the height of the dot-com bubble, when tech stocks outperformed the S&P 500 by 253%, today's 44% outperformance seems modest. Despite the downgrade, Lerner emphasized that Truist is still bullish on tech for the long term. He believes that AI will be a durable driver of growth in the sector going into the future. Lerner is optimistic that there will be new opportunities to bet on tech outside the Magnificent Seven going forward. \"There will likely be a better opportunity to deploy capital in a meaningful way, and we will be looking for a better entry point to upgrade the sector in the future,\" Lerner wrote in the note. After downgrading tech, Truist is shifting its focus on seeking value below the market's surface. Lerner is bullish on communication services and utilities. Both of these sectors are indirectly benefiting from the AI boom. Telecommunication companies are benefiting from government initiatives to invest in the 5G network infrastructure necessary for training AI models. Utilities have received a boost from surging demand as data centers consume massive amounts of power. Investors can gain exposure to these sectors through funds like the SPDR S&P Telecom ETF (XTL), iShares US Telecommunications ETF (IYZ), the Utilities Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLU), and Vanguard Utilities Index Fund ETF (VPU).","articleSection":"Markets","isAccessibleForFree":false,"hasPart":[{"@type":"WebPageElement","isAccessibleForFree":false,"cssSelector":"[data-lock-content]"}]}
